# Disagreement Log — Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 19

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 28

---

## Disagreements

**v. 1** — "God foreknew even their future" (EMET) vs. "God foreknew what they would yet do" (LOGOS) vs. "God already knew what they would do" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 2** — "having themselves permitted the departure of the Israelites" (EMET) vs. "having themselves permitted the departure" (LOGOS — more concise) vs. "would themselves permit the Israelites to leave" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 2** — "sent them forth with great urgency" (EMET) vs. "sent the Israelites forth with urgency" (LOGOS) vs. "would even press them to go with urgency" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 3** — "took up another senseless plan" (EMET) vs. "conceived another foolish plan" (LOGOS) vs. "reached a fresh foolish decision" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 3** — "those whom they had expelled with entreaties" (EMET) vs. "those whom they had driven out with entreaties" (LOGOS) vs. "the people they had just expelled with urgent pleas" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "the fate that they deserved was drawing them to this end" (EMET) vs. "the fate they deserved was drawing them to this end" (LOGOS) vs. "the fate that was rightfully theirs was pulling them toward exactly this end" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "complete the punishment which was still lacking to their torments" (EMET) vs. "fill up the gap still left in their punishment by further torments" (LOGOS) vs. "fill what was still lacking in their punishment" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "fill up the punishment still lacking in their torments."

**v. 5** — "pass through the water by a miraculous way" (EMET) vs. "journey through the water by a miraculous way" (LOGOS) vs. "pass through the sea by a way that defied all reason" (PNEUMA — changes "water" to "sea" and adds interpretation). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 5** — "strange death" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "death utterly unlike anything before" (PNEUMA — expands). EMET/LOGOS preferred.

**v. 6** — "fashioned anew, serving your specific commands" (EMET) vs. "refashioned anew, serving your distinct commands" (LOGOS) vs. "remade in its natural order, freshly rearranged, obedient to your specific commands" (PNEUMA — expands). SOPHIA: "fashioned anew, serving your distinct commands."

**v. 7** — "dry land arising where water had been before" (EMET) vs. "dry land appeared where water had been before" (LOGOS) vs. "dry land rising where water had been" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 7** — "open road out of the Red Sea" (EMET) vs. "out of the Red Sea an unobstructed road" (LOGOS) vs. "out of the Red Sea, an open road" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 7** — "grassy plain out of the violent surge" (EMET) vs. "grassy plain out of the raging flood" (LOGOS) vs. "level grassy plain" (PNEUMA — omits source detail). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 9** — "grazed like horses" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "frolicked like horses turned out to pasture" (PNEUMA — expands). EMET/LOGOS preferred.

**v. 9** — "leaped about like lambs" (EMET) vs. "skipped like lambs" (LOGOS) vs. "leaped like lambs at play" (PNEUMA — adds "at play"). EMET preferred.

**v. 10** — "things of their sojourn" (EMET) vs. "what had happened in their sojourn" (LOGOS) vs. "what it had been like in Egypt" (PNEUMA — specifies "Egypt," not in text). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 11** — "a new birth of birds" (EMET) vs. "a new kind of bird" (LOGOS) vs. "something new entirely — a fresh kind of bird" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 11** — "carried by craving" (EMET) vs. "led on by appetite" (LOGOS) vs. "their hunger drove them" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 12** — "quails came up from the sea for them" (EMET) vs. "quails came up from the sea for their nourishment" (LOGOS) vs. "quails came rising up from the sea" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 13** — "prior signs given in the violence of thunder" (EMET) vs. "prior warnings given through the violence of thunder" (LOGOS) vs. "the thunder had already announced it" (PNEUMA — condenses). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 13** — "more bitter hatred toward strangers" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "more savage hatred toward outsiders" (PNEUMA). EMET/LOGOS: "strangers" preferred to PNEUMA's "outsiders."

**v. 14** — "did not receive strangers who were unknown to them" (EMET) vs. "refused to receive strangers they had never known" (LOGOS) vs. "merely refused entry to strangers they did not know" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 14** — "enslaved guests who were their benefactors" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "enslaved guests who had done nothing but bless them" (PNEUMA — interpretive). EMET/LOGOS preferred.

**v. 15** — "will be some other judgment for the others" (EMET) vs. "will be a particular accounting for those others" (LOGOS) vs. "separate accounting for those earlier sinners" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "a particular accounting" (LOGOS).

**v. 16** — "welcomed them with festivity" (EMET) vs. "welcomed the Israelites with celebrations" (LOGOS) vs. "welcomed them with festivals" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 18** — "the elements rearranged themselves with one another, just as the notes on a harp vary the character of the melody while the rhythm remains the same" (EMET) vs. "just as on a harp the notes vary the character of the melody while the rhythm is preserved throughout" (LOGOS) vs. PNEUMA elaborates at length. SOPHIA: LOGOS structure with EMET's opening clause.

**v. 21** — "parch the flesh" (EMET) vs. "scorch the flesh" (LOGOS) vs. "sear the flesh" (PNEUMA). "Scorch" preferred.

**v. 21** — "crystalline kind of heavenly food" (EMET) vs. "ice-like kind of heavenly nourishment" (LOGOS) vs. "ice-like crystals of manna" (PNEUMA — adds "manna"). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 22** — "magnified and glorified your people" (EMET) vs. "exalted and glorified your people" (LOGOS) vs. "exalted your people and wrapped them in glory" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: EMET's "magnified" for ἐμεγάλυνας retained.
